info.title: Managed DATA ORCHESTRATOR API
info.description:
Welcome to the Scaleway **Data Orchestrator** API. Data Orchestrator is designed to help you automate, schedule, and manage data workflows across various systems and environments. It is vendor-neutral and open-source, as it is based on the [Open Workflow Specification](https://open-workflow-specification.org/).

A **workflow** is a structured sequence of action and logic tasks that defines an end-to-end data process. You define the workflow once, and Data Orchestrator takes care of running it reliably and gives you full visibility on every execution.

<Message type="note">
Data Orchestrator is currently in **Public Beta**. During this Beta period, workflows run Scaleway Serverless Jobs, Serverless Functions, Serverless Containers, HTTP calls, Object Storage, and Generative API.
</Message>

## Concepts

### Workflow definition

A **Workflow definition** is the declarative blueprint of a workflow, typically described in YAML. It specifies the tasks, dependencies, conditions and execution parameters, and holds the workflow DSL, its environment variables and an optional cron schedule. It is version-controlled, reusable and portable across environments.

### Workflow version

A **Workflow version** is a versioned snapshot of a workflow definition. Workflow definitions are versioned so you can evolve your workflow while keeping full control over which version is executed. The `is_current` flag designates the version selected to run.

### Workflow run

A **Workflow run** is the runtime instance of a workflow definition. It tracks the state, logs and results of every task, providing full observability and auditability. Runs can succeed, fail or be paused, with detailed insights for debugging.

### Task

A **task** is a unit of work inside a workflow. Two categories of tasks exist:

- **Action tasks** perform concrete work: **Serverless Jobs** (long-running batch processes), **Serverless Functions** (lightweight event-driven code), **Serverless Containers**, **HTTP calls**, **Object Storage** and **Generative API**.
- **Logic tasks** control the flow and decision-making within a workflow: **Switch**, **Fork** and **Try-catch**.

### Trigger

A **trigger** is the event that initiates a workflow run. Triggers can be:

- **Manual** — the run is started by the user via the console or the API (ideal for testing).
- **Schedule** — automatic execution based on time, set with a cron expression and its timezone.

## Getting started

1. Make sure you have a Scaleway account and an [API key](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/iam/how-to/create-api-keys/) with the necessary IAM permissions, and export your credentials:

    ```bash
    export SCW_SECRET_KEY="<API secret key>"
    export SCW_DEFAULT_REGION="fr-par"
    export SCW_PROJECT_ID="<Scaleway Project ID>"
    ```

2. **Create a workflow definition**: a workflow definition holds the workflow DSL and its configuration:

    ```bash
    curl -X POST \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      "https://api.scaleway.com/data-orchestrator/v1alpha2/regions/$SCW_DEFAULT_REGION/workflow-definitions" \
      -d '{
        "name": "my-first-workflow",
        "project_id": "'"$SCW_PROJECT_ID"'",
        "workflow_version": {
          "name": "v1",
          "workflow_dsl": "version: 1.0.3\nname: my-first-workflow\n"
        }
      }'
    ```

3. **Start a workflow run** on your definition:

    ```bash
    curl -X POST \
      -H "X-Auth-Token: $SCW_SECRET_KEY" \
      "https://api.scaleway.com/data-orchestrator/v1alpha2/regions/$SCW_DEFAULT_REGION/workflow-definitions/<workflow-definition-id>/start"
    ```

4. **Follow your run**: list your workflow runs and inspect their status, task runs and output.

## Technical information

### Availability

The Data Orchestrator API is regional. It is available in the following region:

- **Paris** — `fr-par`

## Going further

For more information about Data Orchestrator, check out:

- Our [Data Orchestrator documentation](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/data-orchestrator/)
- The [Data Orchestrator Quickstart](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/data-orchestrator/quickstart/)
- The [Open Workflow Specification](https://open-workflow-specification.org/) used for the workflow DSL.
